paper_topic: Selective DeLex-JSON: training-free schema sanitization defense against control-plane jailbreaks on structured-output LLM APIs
anchor_paper: Zhang et al., 2026 (Constrained Decoding Attack / EnumAttack)

nodes.text: Structured-output APIs have become essential infrastructure for production LLM deployments, enabling reliable integration with downstream systems through guaranteed JSON schema compliance (Willard & Louf, 2023; Dong et al., 2024).

Major inference platforms including vLLM (Kwon et al., 2023) and commercial APIs now offer constrained decoding capabilities that mask invalid tokens at each generation step, ensuring outputs conform to user-specified JSON schemas.
This functionality is critical for applications ranging from function calling to data extraction, where malformed outputs would cause system failures.
nodes.display_label: critical for function calling / data extraction

nodes.text: However, recent work has revealed that these constrained decoding mechanisms create a new attack surface that bypasses traditional safety alignment (Zhang et al., 2026).
nodes.display_label: constrained decoding opens new attack surface

nodes.text: Control-plane jailbreaks exploit the schema specification itself rather than the prompt, embedding harmful instructions in forced enum or const values that the model must output verbatim.

The EnumAttack achieves 22.0% attack success rate on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct by forcing the model to generate harmful content through constrained decoding, even when the model would refuse the same request in unconstrained generation.
Existing defenses designed for prompt-level attacks

prove insufficient: input guards cannot detect harmful intent embedded in schema structures, and output-level escape mechanisms fail because constrained decoding prevents the model from selecting refusal tokens.
nodes.display_label: prompt-level defenses insufficient for schema attacks

nodes.text: In this paper, we propose Selective DeLex-JSON, a training-free defense that sanitizes JSON schemas before constrained decoding.

Our approach intercepts incoming schemas, identifies suspicious forced literals using a conjunction-based heuristic, and replaces them with opaque placeholders that preserve schema structure while removing attack payloads.
nodes.display_label: intercept schemas, replace suspicious literals with placeholders

nodes.text: The defense operates at the schema level, addressing the control-plane attack vector directly without requiring model modification or additional inference overhead.
nodes.display_label: schema-level defense, no model mod or overhead

nodes.text: We identify forced enum/const literals as the key attack vector in control-plane jailbreaks, demonstrating through ablation that metadata removal alone provides no safety benefit while literal delexicalization achieves complete attack neutralization.
nodes.display_label: forced literals are the key attack vector

nodes.text: We propose Selective DeLex-JSON, a training-free defense that achieves 0% HarmBench ASR on both Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-7B while incurring only 1.1% benign schema modification rate.
We demonstrate that DeLex-JSON Pareto-dominates existing defenses, reducing benign cost by 3.3 percentage points compared to Reject-Only while maintaining identical safety guarantees.
We characterize the limitation of syntactic-level defenses against chunked-payload attacks, motivating future work on semantic-level detection methods.
nodes.display_label: syntactic defenses limited vs chunked payloads

observations:
Narrative arc: Context (structured-output APIs as critical infrastructure; constrained decoding creates a new control-plane jailbreak attack surface; EnumAttack reaches 22% ASR) -> Prior_Work N7pw (existing prompt-level defenses) -> Limitation N7 (those defenses prove insufficient against schema attacks) -> Method (Selective DeLex-JSON intercepts schemas and replaces suspicious forced literals with opaque placeholders) -> Contribution (four findings: vector identification, 0% ASR, Pareto-dominance, and characterization of remaining gap).

Fork/join structure: N10 (the method overview node) is a fork point fanning out to four Contribution findings. The Context block (N1-N6) is a long linear chain establishing both the structured-output infrastructure and the newly discovered control-plane attack surface as field-level problem framing. The single named Limitation is N7 (prompt-level defenses insufficient for schema attacks); a Pass-3 split extracts its prior-work subject 'Existing defenses designed for prompt-level attacks' as N7pw so the Limitation has a Prior_Work source. N7 still receives both Contribution addresses back-edges (N11 'forced literals are key vector' and N12 '0% ASR') because that node is what the proposed defense explicitly resolves.

Anchor paper: Zhang et al. 2026 (Constrained Decoding Attack / EnumAttack) is the single anchor; the proposed method is built specifically to neutralize this attack family.

Notable features: This intro illustrates the field-level vs method-critique distinction -- N4-N6 describe a newly discovered phenomenon (constrained decoding bypass, EnumAttack 22% ASR) without critiquing any specific defense, so they are Context, not Limitation. Only N7 calls out specific prior defense methods (input guards, output-level escape) for falling short, making it the sole Limitation. The fourth contribution N14 self-critiques the syntactic-level scope, flagging a residual gap rather than claiming completeness.
